mainTopic: Three sisters who fall for יבום before two brothers: רב's ruling built on יש זיקה and חליצה פסולה, the one-after-another explanation, and שמואל's opposing view
overview: This amud opens by finishing the previous discussion: we take into account that one brother might die, but not that two brothers will die. Then רב, quoted by רבא בר רב הונא, rules on three sisters who fall for יבום before two brothers. Each brother does חליצה with one sister, and the third sister needs חליצה from both. רבה explains that this must assume יש זיקה, so her חליצה is a חליצה פסולה that has to be repeated with every brother. The גמרא then asks why the first two sisters do not need both brothers as well. It answers that רב means sisters who fell one after another: the first two get a proper חליצה, and only the last one's חליצה is flawed. The גמרא asks how רב can say this when he holds אין זיקה, and answers that he was speaking according to those who hold יש זיקה. Finally, שמואל rules that one brother's חליצה is enough for each sister. The גמרא begins to challenge him from his own statement that a proper חליצה is required, and the quote of that statement comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not worry in a case of five brothers too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier reasoning. If we worry that a brother might die, that worry should also apply when there are five brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the same should be true with five brothers as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the discussion from just before this section. It argues that the earlier worry should also apply to a case with five brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא explained a ruling by worrying that one of the remaining brothers might die. If that worry is real, the same reasoning should stretch to a case of five brothers, where two of them married two sisters and died. If the worry applies there too, the rule should be the same, and the גמרא wants to know why it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Five (here, five brothers)
Also, too. Used to say the same reasoning should apply to another case

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the tail end of the discussion that came right before this section, so it only makes sense as a reply to that earlier reasoning.

phrases.english: Five as well!
phrases.notes: He means a case of five brothers, two married to two sisters who died, leaving three brothers. The same worry should apply there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries on the discussion from just before this section by testing its reasoning on a case with more brothers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation that relied on the worry that a brother might die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the worry that a brother may die is enough to change the ruling, it should also change the ruling in a case of five brothers.

steps.title: We do not worry that two brothers will die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we worry that one brother might die, but we do not worry that two brothers will die.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are not concerned that two of them will die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Worrying that one brother might die is reasonable, but worrying that two will die is too far-fetched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of five brothers would only become a problem if two of the remaining brothers died. חז"ל take into account the realistic chance that one person might die. They do not make rules based on the unlikely chance that two people will die. So the five-brother case is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Death
We are not concerned; we do not take this possibility into account

steps.whatToRemember: We take into account the chance that one brother might die, but not the chance that two will die. That is why the worry does not extend to five brothers.

phrases.english: For the death of two, we are not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by limiting how far the worry goes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the worry: one death is taken into account, two deaths are not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry that a brother might die should apply to any number of brothers, including five.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the chance of one brother dying is taken into account. The five-brother case would need two deaths, so we ignore it.

steps.title: רב's ruling on three sisters and two brothers
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא quotes רב. If three sisters fall for יבום before two brothers, each brother does חליצה with one sister, and the third sister needs חליצה from both brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב הונא said in the name of רב: if three sisters became יבמות and fell before two brothers who are their יבמין, this brother does חליצה with one, that brother does חליצה with one, and the middle one needs חליצה from both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב rules on a case where three sisters, widowed from three brothers, fall before only two remaining brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each brother does חליצה with one sister. The third sister, called the "middle" one, needs חליצה from both brothers, not just one. רב does not give a reason here. The next steps work out what reason must lie behind it and which situation he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Widows who must do יבום or חליצה with their late husband's brother
The surviving brothers who are tied to the widows for יבום
Does חליצה, the ceremony that releases the widow without יבום
The middle one; here, the third sister

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Three sisters who are yevamot
phrases.notes: They were married to three brothers who all died, so all three are now waiting for יבום.

phrases.english: who fell before two brothers who are their yevamin
this one does chalitza with one
and that one does chalitza with one,
and the middle one needs chalitza from both of them.
phrases.notes: "Middle" here just means the remaining third sister, the one left over after each brother released one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching after the five-brothers exchange ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three sisters before two brothers: each brother does חליצה with one sister, and the third sister needs חליצה from both brothers.

steps.title: רבה explains the reasoning behind רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבה works out what רב must hold. Requiring חליצה from both brothers means רב holds יש זיקה, so the third sister's חליצה is a חליצה פסולה, and a חליצה פסולה must be repeated with every brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: since you say the middle one needs חליצה from both, you must hold יש זיקה. Her חליצה is then a חליצה פסולה, and a חליצה פסולה must go around to all the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains the reason that must be behind רב's ruling. He is setting up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the third sister need חליצה from both brothers? It must be because רב holds יש זיקה: the bond of יבום makes each sister count like a relative's sister to the brother. So she is forbidden to him for יבום, and a חליצה done with a woman who cannot do יבום is a חליצה פסולה. A חליצה פסולה does not fully release her, so every brother must do חליצה with her.

keyTerms.meaning: The view that the bond of יבום is strong and counts almost like a real marriage tie
A flawed חליצה, done with a woman who could not do יבום; it does not fully release her
You must hold (an inference about someone's view)
To go around to all the brothers, so that each one does חליצה

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not disagreeing yet. First he lays out the reasoning רב's ruling depends on. The actual challenge comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
From the fact that you say the middle one needs chalitza from both of them,
you must hold there is a levirate bond,
and so it becomes a flawed chalitza —

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲלִיצָה פְּסוּלָה צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר עַל כׇּל הָאַחִין,
phrases.english: and a flawed chalitza must go around to all the brothers,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the reasoning behind רב's ruling in step 3 so it can be challenged.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning behind רב's ruling that the third sister needs חליצה from both brothers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It lays out the principles רב's ruling depends on (יש זיקה, חליצה פסולה, repeating it with all brothers), so the next step can show they lead further than רב said.

steps.title: Then the first two sisters should need חליצה from both brothers too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the reasoning is יש זיקה, then the first two sisters' חליצות are also flawed, so they should also need חליצה from both brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the first ones as well!
steps.whatsHappening: Using the reasoning רבה just laid out, the גמרא challenges רב's ruling. The same logic should apply to the first two sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first brother did חליצה with the first sister, the other sisters were also tied to him, so she too was the sister of a woman tied to him. That makes her חליצה flawed in the same way. So the first two sisters should also need חליצה from both brothers, and not just the third one. רב only said this about the third sister, so his ruling does not seem to fit his own reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a challenge built on what was just said
The first ones; here, the first two sisters

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge tests whether יש זיקה can explain רב's ruling at all. If the bond makes the third sister's חליצה flawed, it seems to make every sister's חליצה flawed.

phrases.english: If so, the first ones as well!
phrases.notes: He means the first two sisters. Each was also the sister of a woman tied to that brother, so their חליצה is flawed too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning laid out in step 4 to challenge רב's ruling from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that only the third sister needs חליצה from both brothers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under יש זיקה, each of the first two sisters was also the sister of a woman tied to the brother who released her. So their חליצה is also flawed and should also need to be repeated with both brothers.

steps.title: The sisters fell one after another
steps.stepSummary: If all three sisters fell at once, all three would indeed need חליצה from both brothers. רב's case is when they fell one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they fell at the same time, that is true. The case is needed only where they fell one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5. It agrees with the question in one situation and says רב was talking about a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא asked why the first two sisters' חליצות are not also flawed. The גמרא answers: if all three fell together, they would be, so all three would need both brothers. רב's ruling is about sisters who fell in order, one after the other, and that order changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: At the same time
Indeed, so it is (agreeing with the challenger)
It is needed only for (this specific case)
One after the other

phrases.english: If they fell at the same time,
phrases.notes: "Fell" means the sisters came before the brothers for יבום, because their husbands died.

phrases.english: indeed, that is so.
The ruling is needed only
where they fell one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דִּנְפוּל בְּבַת אַחַת הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 5 by narrowing רב's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): sisters falling one after another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's case had all three sisters falling together, so the first two sisters should also need both brothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב is talking about sisters who fell one after another, so only the last one has a flawed חליצה.

steps.title: Working through the order of the sisters
steps.stepSummary: ראובן does a proper חליצה with the first sister and שמעון with the second. The third sister's חליצה is flawed for each brother, so each one only ends his own bond with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: One sister fell, and Reuven did חליצה with her. Another fell, and Shimon did חליצה with her. Another fell: when this brother does חליצה with her, he ends only his own bond, and when that brother does חליצה with her, he ends only his own bond.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא walks through the case step by step to show why only the third sister needs חליצה from both brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When ראובן does חליצה with the first sister, she is fully released from both brothers, so שמעון's חליצה with the second sister is proper. The third sister is the sister of a woman each brother did חליצה with, so each brother's חליצה with her is a חליצה פסולה. A flawed חליצה only ends that brother's own זיקה, so she needs חליצה from both.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one, another one
He did חליצה with her
He ends his own bond (only his, not his brother's)
A flawed חליצה that does not fully release the woman

steps.whatToRemember: Order matters. The early sisters get a proper חליצה that frees them from everyone. Only the last sister, who is the sister of women already released by חליצה, gets a flawed חליצה. That is why she needs both brothers.

phrases.english: One fell, and Reuven did חליצה with her;
another fell, and Shimon did חליצה with her;
another one fell:
when this brother does חליצה with her, he ends his own bond,
and when that brother does חליצה with her, he ends his own bond.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the one-after-another case from Step 6 and shows how it answers the challenge of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the case step by step
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three sisters' חליצות are flawed under יש זיקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the third sister's חליצה is flawed, so only she needs חליצה from both brothers.

steps.title: But רב holds there is no זיקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this ruling, which depends on יש זיקה, can come from רב, who said אין זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say: there is no זיקה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole explanation. It is built on יש זיקה, but רב himself holds the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling only makes sense if the woman waiting for יבום is tied to each brother. רב is known to hold אין זיקה, that there is no such tie. So it seems strange that רב would give a ruling that depends on זיקה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say (a challenge from someone's own words elsewhere)
There is no real bond between the woman and the brothers before יבום

phrases.english: But didn't רב say:
there is no זיקה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the יש זיקה basis that Steps 4 to 7 used to explain רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining רב's ruling with יש זיקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב elsewhere holds אין זיקה, so his ruling cannot depend on יש זיקה.

steps.title: רב was speaking according to the other view
steps.stepSummary: רב gave this ruling according to the view that holds יש זיקה, not according to his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was speaking according to the one who says there is זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב was not giving his own opinion here. He was explaining what the law would be for someone who holds יש זיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב personally holds אין זיקה, and by his view the third sister would not need both brothers. He was teaching how the case works out for those who hold יש זיקה. So there is no contradiction between his two statements.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words of the one who says
There is a real bond between the woman and each brother
He is saying

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbi can teach a ruling based on someone else's opinion. רב holds אין זיקה, but his ruling about the three sisters follows the יש זיקה view.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that רב changed his mind. He still holds אין זיקה. This ruling was only explaining the other view.

phrases.english: According to the words of the one who says there is זיקה
he was speaking.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling shows רב's own view, which contradicts his statement אין זיקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was explaining the law for those who hold יש זיקה, while he himself holds אין זיקה.

steps.title: שמואל: one brother's חליצה is enough for each sister
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. In the case of the three sisters, it is enough for one brother to do חליצה with each sister, including the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: one brother does חליצה for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings שמואל's opinion on the same case of three sisters who fell to two brothers. He says the third sister does not need חליצה from both brothers. One is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the third sister needed חליצה from both brothers, because her חליצה from each one was flawed. שמואל says one brother's חליצה is enough for every sister, so the third sister is treated like the first two.

keyTerms.meaning: One brother does the חליצה
For all of them, here meaning each of the sisters

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a new dispute with רב and leads straight into the next challenge.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
One brother performs ḥalitza for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that disagrees with רב's ruling on the case discussed in steps 6-9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of three sisters who fall to two יבמין, one brother's חליצה is enough for each sister.

steps.title: But שמואל requires a complete, proper חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל can call one brother's חליצה enough here. Elsewhere he said a flawed חליצה does not fully free the woman. The source of his view is about to be quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, we have heard that שמואל said we need a complete, proper חליצה, for שמואל said: (quote follows).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against שמואל's ruling, using another statement of his own. It is setting up a quote, which comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third sister's חליצה is flawed because she is the sister of a woman each brother already released with חליצה, so neither brother could do יבום with her (step 7). If שמואל holds that only a proper חליצה fully frees a woman, one brother's flawed חליצה should not be enough for her. His two statements seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (opens a point the listener already knows)
We have heard him say
A complete, proper חליצה
We require

steps.confusionAlert: The line ends with 'שמואל said:' and stops. The actual statement of שמואל is quoted right after this line, so do not look for it here.

phrases.english: Now, since we have heard that Shmuel
said: We require a full-fledged ḥalitza,
as Shmuel said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 10 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one brother's חליצה is enough for each sister, including the third.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: שמואל requires a complete, proper חליצה, but the third sister's חליצה from one brother is flawed, so it should not be enough.
